title: paged kv cache: block allocator reuse + pinning improvements
author: Aisha Patel
description: Motivation: reduce allocator contention and tail-latency caused by frequent block allocations and premature eviction of hot KV blocks. This PR implements block allocator reuse across requests, a lightweight pinning API for hot blocks, and conservative eviction hints to reduce churn. We also add unit tests, microbenchmarks, and an end-to-end perf regression test. Key changes: 1) BlockAllocator: add a recycled pool for small/fixed-size blocks with atomic free lists to reduce malloc churn and lock contention; 2) BlockPinning: expose pin/unpin calls to pin hot prefix blocks during long-running chat sessions; 3) EvictionHints: track hotness metadata and prefer retaining pinned/recently-used blocks during GC; 4) Metrics and tracing: new metrics (kv.block_recycles, kv.pin_count, kv.eviction_skipped) and tracing spans around allocation/eviction hotspots; 5) Tests/benchmarks: new microbench that simulates 1000 concurrent streams with skewed prefix reuse and shows 9-12% p50 latency improvement and 28% lower allocation rate. Backwards compatibility: pin/unpin is optional and defaults to no-op for code paths that don't opt-in. Rollout plan: feature gated behind runtime flag kv_pinning_enabled and gradual rollout on dedicated clusters. Related PRs: #21089, #20321, #19510.

review_comments: Liam Chen: Can you explain the choice of atomic freelist vs thread-local caches? Concern about ABA on 64-bit targets.
Aisha Patel: Chose atomic freelist to keep memory bounded and simpler to integrate with existing block lifecycle; added a tagged pointer to mitigate ABA and unit tests to exercise races.
María González: Need stronger safety doc for pin/unpin semantics; what happens if a connection dies while blocks are pinned?

Aisha Patel: Pin is ref-counted at block level; we added a background reaper that unpins after a soft timeout and metrics to surface leaked pins. Added docs section explaining behavior and recommended usage patterns.
Ethan Brooks: CI flake on macOS allocator test — looks like an async ordering issue in the test harness.
Aisha Patel: Reproduced locally; updated test to use barrier and added flake repro yaml. Rerunning CI.
María González: Approve after tests and docs updates.
Liam Chen: Minor nit: rename kv.block_recycles -> kv.block_recycles_total for prometheus conventions.
Aisha Patel: Renamed metric and pushed.
release_notes: Performance: Block allocator reuse and pinning reduce allocation churn and improve tail latency for workloads with hot prefix reuse. Opt-in via runtime flag kv_pinning_enabled. See docs/runtime/kv_pinning.md for details.
performance_summary: Microbench simulating 1000 concurrent streams with skewed prefix reuse shows 9-12% improvement in p50 latency and 18% improvement in p95; allocation rate reduced by ~28% and memory churn reduced leading to fewer GC events.
